Patskanyovo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Patskanyovo, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century, this cemetery existed by 1880 per epigraphic data, presumably used until WWII, though its latest preserved gravestone dates to 1936. Jews are believed to have arrived in the 19th century; population reached 8 by 1830 and 40 (4%) by 1880, rising to 129 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). Some Jews farmed small plots while others operated two flour mills and several inns, or worked as administrative officials; local youth were active in Zionist organizations and Agudat Israel. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; population reached 106 by 1941, when some Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Some Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; remaining Patskanyovo Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
